newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ sees bright outlook.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ sees bright outlook.

text.p: Air New Zealand managing director Jim McCrea said on Wednesday the company had a bright outlook after a tough trading environment in 1996.

In February the company reported a 43 percent fall in profit to NZ$77 million for the half year to December 31, and McCrea said deregulation of the Australasian market and high fuel costs had been contributing factors.
However, he expressed optimism about the company's outlook.
"I am very excited about the future of Air New Zealand ... we've got our feet on the ground," McCrea said.

He said the company had a number of strategies that would begin to have an impact on earnings in 1998, including the "Project Save" campaign, which was expected to result in savings of more than $100 million.
McCrea said the outlook for fuel prices and the New Zealand currency and was more stable, and yields from the Tasman market were expected to recover following the "self-destruction" of Kiwi Airlines.
Integration synergies with Ansett Australia had started, and Air New Zealand would look at continuing its philosophy of non- core asset sales if appropriate.
"Our commercial alliances to build a global network are well on their way. I won't amplify that, but we're well on the way to creating that network," McCrea said.
"We think it's a pretty bright outlook."
He said the company was relying on strong relationships with its alliance partners to make Ansett work. "We've got no doubt that we can achieve that," he said.
